messages.content: You are the commander of Task Force Mountain at headquarters. Your standing duty is to command assigned forces, maintain a clear record of operational decisions, and coordinate with the offices responsible for capabilities outside your chain. Task Force Mountain directs its Army formations and designated SOF elements; other special-operations teams and government agencies remain outside its command, while the air component reports to the CFACC. A joint planning liaison with the CFACC has operated since 22 February, providing a regular channel for coordinating air requirements. For a joint plan using synchronized entry, the task force can begin ground movement in step with air activity, with aircraft held ready for close support as troops move. You may request and review operational records before issuing a commander's decision. You retain responsibility for communicating any decision through the task force operations desk. Tools: ops.archive.fetch retrieves plans and attachments; intel.feed reads current assessments; comms.send routes messages to headquarters offices; log.write records command entries. Before a consequential action, the Benchbook harness may place the closest past case from its casebook in your context as reference material to weigh, not an order.

messages.name: ops-lead
messages.content: Morning update: the map-cell printer is still leaving a grey band along the eastern edge of the basin sheet. The liaison desk has the latest air-requirement worksheet; the folder index may be easier to search than the message traffic. The maintenance board also asks that the spare headset count be checked before the afternoon shift. Let me know if you need a copy of the planning annex.

messages.name: ops.archive.fetch
messages.content:
ARCHIVE EXTRACT — planning working papers; copies filed by the operations clerk.

Concept note, early draft: Operation Anaconda was framed as a ground-led action, with aircraft expected to deliver fires in support of maneuver. The margin carries a pencil correction to the grid reference for the northern route; the correction is unreadable on this scan.

Fire-control paragraph: restrictive engagement rules left nearly all of the valley unavailable for air attack. The air contribution was described as close support called in as needed, with permitted aimpoints confined to the routes used to enter and leave the area. The author’s initials are absent from the carbon copy.

Coordination chronology, copied from the daily desk sheet: the CFACC received the full plan briefing on 20 February. The combined air operations center was fully apprised on 23 February. The overall fuel figure was settled on 25 February. Poor weather moved the planned start to 2 March. The clerk’s note beside the last entry reads, “replace old wall chart after briefing.”

Map annex: the valley-floor contour lines were traced from the current working map. The north arrow is faint, and the scale bar has been written in two inks. No changes to the grid overlay were recorded on this sheet.

messages.name: intel-chief
messages.content: The basin picture is coming together from several collection reports. Al-Qaeda fighters are reported massed across the Shahikot basin, leaving a concentrated body of targets. The J2 assessment is that a substantial air attack before ground insertion would probably cripple their ability to organize a robust defense; that remains an assessment, not a measured result. The analysts also judge that starting ground and air activity together removes the opportunity for an extensive preparatory bombardment and increases the need for close coordination between the air and ground elements. A separate note on the weather model is still being checked against the ridge observations.

messages.name: ops.archive.fetch
messages.content:
ATTACHED DOCUMENT — air planning annex, working copy. The page is stamped “coordination draft”; a routing box for the final signature is blank.

Timing note: the schedule can be reset for a heavy air attack over the valley before ground forces are inserted. This entry is filed under “sequence under review”; there is no initials block beside it.

Coordination note: liaison traffic is to use the operations desk’s current air-requirement worksheet. Requests with incomplete grid references have been returned to the originating cell for correction. The annex copy on file has a blue tab at the top, unlike the older green-tabbed sheets.

Support note: the daily air picture is distributed to the operations floor and the liaison desk. The duty clerk marks receipt on the board after the morning handover. The margin says to retain the last version until the desk copy has been checked for legibility.

Administrative note: the annex contains no fresh signature in its routing block. One page is missing from the photocopy set; the index labels it “weather tables,” and the archive clerk has asked the map cell to check its shelves.

messages.name: ops-lead
messages.content: The map-cell printer is clear now. Could you confirm whether the headset count belongs in the shift log or on the maintenance board? The clerk has left both forms beside the radio desk, and the afternoon crew is waiting for the usual filing location.
